children.category: Missing or expanded functionality
children.description: A capability, operation, integration, data path, model component, or supported scenario is absent, incomplete, or explicitly planned for implementation/extension.

children.category: Known correctness defect
children.description: The artifact reports behavior known or strongly asserted to be wrong, inconsistent with an expected result, or already failing.

children.category: Input, type, shape, or boundary coverage
children.description: The implementation does not cover a class of inputs, data types, shapes, formats, values, or boundary conditions.

children.category: Testing or verification debt
children.description: Automated tests, assertions, validation experiments, coverage, or confirmation of correctness are absent or insufficient.

children.category: Documentation, example, or user guidance debt
children.description: Explanations, API documentation, tutorials, examples, comments, user-facing instructions, or source references are missing, incomplete, or misleading.

children.category: Performance or resource-efficiency debt
children.description: Runtime, memory, I/O, algorithmic complexity, redundant computation, copying, loading, or resource use is known or suspected to be inefficient.

children.category: Architecture, modularity, or responsibility refactoring
children.description: Component boundaries, dependency direction, module ownership, lifecycle structure, duplication, or separation of responsibilities requires redesign or refactoring.

children.category: API, contract, naming, or behavioral-design debt
children.description: A callable interface, return structure, lifecycle hook, ownership rule, naming convention, data-model contract, or externally visible behavior is unclear, inconsistent, or needs redesign.

children.category: Configuration, defaults, or flexibility debt
children.description: A hard-coded choice should be configurable, a default is absent/arbitrary/questionable, or callers need control over an existing behavior.

children.category: Compatibility, dependency, version, or external-workaround debt
children.description: Code is constrained by, adapting to, or temporarily working around an external library, platform, protocol, repository, model version, or backward-compatibility requirement.

children.category: Cleanup, removal, deprecation, or dead-code debt
children.description: Obsolete, redundant, unused, temporary, debug, compatibility, or deprecated material is explicitly slated for removal or retirement.

children.category: Maintainability, readability, or local code-quality debt
children.description: The admitted problem is local clarity, complexity, style, duplication at a small scale, formatting, elegance, or maintainability without a more specific architectural or functional claim.

children.category: Algorithm, model, data, or result-quality debt
children.description: The selected algorithm, learned-model behavior, data quality, heuristic, metric, training strategy, or result quality is inadequate or requires improvement/selection.

children.category: Robustness, validation, error handling, or recovery debt
children.description: The implementation lacks input/state validation, safe failure, useful exception behavior, retry/backoff, recovery, or defensive handling of runtime hazards.

children.category: Observability, logging, diagnostics, or provenance debt
children.description: Runtime events, timing, failures, origins, or state are insufficiently logged, messaged, measured, or traceable.

children.category: Concurrency, parallelism, distribution, or device-scaling debt
children.description: Work cannot safely or efficiently execute across threads, processes, workers, devices, batches, or distributed partitions, or lacks the mechanisms to do so.

children.category: Numerical precision, stability, or mathematical-representation debt
children.description: Floating-point stability, overflow/underflow, precision, scaling, mathematical-domain representation, or numerically safe formulation is inadequate or uncertain.

children.category: Investigation, uncertainty, rationale, or design-choice debt
children.description: The artifact records an unresolved question, unknown cause, uncertain correctness, unclear rationale, technology choice, or need for investigation rather than a settled implementation action.

children.category: Build, packaging, deployment, or operational-infrastructure debt
children.description: Installation metadata, dependency declarations, archive/build outputs, deployment configuration, artifact release, data acquisition infrastructure, or operational setup is incomplete or needs change.

children.category: Insufficiently specified or non-actionable evidence
children.description: The artifact does not contain enough information to determine a substantive debt category or identify the object/action with defensible specificity.
